title: Connection queue collapse during escalations — fastpatch and cross-env mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a customer escalation window we observed sustained 5xx and long tail timeouts for a subset of customers using streaming/long-poll requests. Impact spanned Hosted and Dedicated fallbacks (Private unaffected unless routing hit Hosted gateway). Symptoms were connection queues on the front-door broker filling with half-open/idle sessions, subsequent synchronous fallback to Dedicated pools, and a synchronized fanout that triggered backend overload and 502/504 responses.

Why this is unique: root cause is a recent change to the admission prioritizer that switched a per-session admission cap to a global ‘soft cap’ without propagating backpressure to the gateway. This combined with mismatched keepalive and idle timeouts across stacked proxies allowed many stale TCP/stream handles to accumulate, blocking the request broker’s processing loop and stalling healthy traffic.

Customer impact: high — several paying customers reported degraded throughput and elevated error rates; some customers hit request-level SLAs. We received direct escalations (CS tickets #CS-7642, #CS-7649).

Goals: 1) immediate mitigation to restore normal request throughput; 2) deploy a backward-compatible runtime patch that reintroduces per-session admission bounds and explicit backpressure propagation; 3) harden fallback behavior to avoid synchronous fanout on overload; 4) update runbooks and SDK guidance to avoid client-side retry amplification in this failure mode.
repro_steps: Use a streaming client that opens many idle streams with infrequent heartbeats (simulate real customer streaming workload).
Apply the admission-prioritizer regression (build from branch candidate with the change).
Throttle the backing inference pool artificially to force fallback to Dedicated. Watch front-door broker connection queue depth and request latency.
Observe synchronous fallback fanout and spike of 502/504 from Dedicated pools when connection queue exceeds processing capacity.
mitigation: Hotfix rolled: temporarily restore previous per-session admission cap on the gateway to stop queue collapse (deployed to Hosted region eu-west-1).
Enabled a temporary soft-limit on Dedicated fallback fanout (max concurrent fallbacks = 8 per front-door instance).
Applied immediate keepalive alignment: lowered proxy idle timeout from 120s to 20s for affected front-door path to clear stale sessions faster.
Customer comms: CS sent targeted notifications and recommended clients reduce aggressive retry/tight backoff settings while we stabilize.
solution_notes: Root fix implemented: admission prioritizer now enforces per-session and per-tenant inflight windows and exposes backpressure signals to the gateway (changes in runtime/admission/controller.go).
Fallback behavior updated: fallbacks are now queued with a randomized jitter and bounded concurrency; a fail-fast cached-response path added for short timeouts to avoid full fanout overload.
Added end-to-end keepalive policy verification in CI with an integration test that simulates half-open streams and verifies queue drain within 2x idle timeout.
Canary: rollout planned across 4-stage canary (10% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) with 30m observation windows and automatic rollback on error-rate delta > 2x baseline.
